content: Glenn Dale Hospital was a tuberculosis sanitarium located in Prince George's County, Maryland, in the United States. Despite its location in Maryland, the property is owned by the government of Washington, D.C. The hospital complex, constructed in 1934, spans 210 acres and consists of 23 buildings. It was closed in 1982 due to the presence of asbestos. Although the facility is no longer operational and is slated for eventual demolition, it served as a significant public health institution for decades, particularly for the Washington, D.C. area. The hospital grounds are regularly patrolled by the Park Police, and a local police officer named Howard Johnson resides on the premises. Officer Johnson has reported various incidents, including apprehending three teenagers from the Annapolis area on October 10, 2007, at 10:10 PM. The site has gained a reputation for being haunted, attracting teenagers and young adults who trespass in search of paranormal activity. Officer Johnson has also confirmed that members of the MS-13 gang and other criminal groups have taken up residence on the property. Additionally, there is an ongoing search for a fugitive wanted for assault who is believed to be hiding within the hospital's 210-acre grounds. Contrary to some rumors, the large incinerator on the property was not used for the disposal of human remains. Instead, it was utilized for burning hospital waste. The hospital complex includes a variety of buildings, each serving specific purposes during its operational years. These buildings include: 1 Four Apartment Building No. 2 Paint Shop Incinerator The buildings are now in a state of significant disrepair, with broken windows, overgrown vegetation, and in some cases, collapsed roofs. The Children's Hospital Building and the Adult Hospital Building are the most frequently explored by trespassers, largely because of their proximity to Glenn Dale Road, a street that cuts through the hospital grounds. These two buildings are connected by a network of underground walkways that link their basements. However, these basements are extremely hazardous, containing sharp, rusted metal debris hanging from the ceilings, as well as large quantities of asbestos. Each basement also houses its own morgue. The underground walkways are now littered with trash, broken glass, and graffiti. Some sections of the walkways are flooded with nearly three feet of water, further adding to the dangers of exploring the site.
